Start from each `Has_amenity` record; combine it with each `Dorm` record for which dormid (`Dorm.dormid`) equals dormid (`Has_amenity.dormid`), one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); group the kept records by dormid (`Has_amenity.dormid`) and gender the dorm admits (`Dorm.gender`); each group gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) dormid (`Has_amenity.dormid`); (2) gender the dorm admits (`Dorm.gender`); (3) the number of records in the group.
Step 2. Start from the rows of step 1; group the kept records by column (2) of step 1; each group gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) column (2) of step 1; (2) the sum of column (3) of step 1 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 3. Start from the rows of step 2; all kept records form one group, which gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) the sum of column (2) of step 2 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 4. Start from the rows of step 2; combine it with the rows of step 3 for which it is not true that column (1) of step 3 is missing, one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); for each kept record, return (1) column (1) of step 2; (2) column (2) of step 2; (3) A ÷ B. Here A is column (2) of step 2; B is column (1) of step 3.
Step 5. Start from the rows of step 4; all kept records form one group, which gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) the average of column (3) of step 4 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 6. Start from the rows of step 4; combine it with the rows of step 5 for which it is not true that column (1) of step 5 is missing, one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); keep only the records for which column (3) of step 4 is greater than column (1) of step 5; for each kept record, return (1) column (1) of step 4; (2) column (2) of step 4; (3) column (3) of step 4; (4) A − B. Here A is column (3) of step 4; B is column (1) of step 5.
Step 7 (the answer). Start from the rows of step 6; all kept records form one group, which gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) the sum of column (2) of step 6 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none); (2) the average of column (3) of step 6 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none); (3) the average of column (4) of step 6 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
